html:
The British and French invasion of German Togoland in August 1914, the first Allied victory of the First World War.

Troops from the Gold Coast and Dahomey, mostly African soldiers, advanced on the great German radio station at Kamina, which linked Berlin to its colonies and its ships in the Atlantic. The Germans blew it up and surrendered on 26 August. Britain and France then divided the colony, and the League of Nations gave each a mandate in 1922. French Togoland became Togo; British Togoland voted in 1956 to join Ghana. The line cut through the lands of the Ewe.
sum: The British and French invasion of German Togoland in August 1914, the first Allied victory of the First World War.
